## Executive Summary

**The "Sooon" tease cashed out as a Black Friday deal.** **@NousResearch**'s 24-hour offer — [**50% off** the first month of **Nous Portal** plans with code **FIFTYFIFTY**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-9714e6d5407e) — drew the batch's biggest reach at **134k+ views** and **893 likes**, and it's the payoff to last cycle's Portal name-drop and "imminent reveal" tease. Two official clarifications matter at checkout: [the exclamation mark is not part of the code](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-b8e764c7f0a0), and [the discount applies to the first month only](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-5175fd109418). If you've been waiting for a cheaper on-ramp to the Portal ecosystem, this is the 24-hour window.

**The Oh My Hermes ecosystem keeps compounding.** **@rlaope**'s **OMH** plugin is nearing [**6.2k GitHub stars**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-86e1892603b8) (up from **6.1k** reported yesterday), and the standout data point is a [power-user report of burning **200B tokens/month** on **Hermes-Agent**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-4db7a63d92b6) through an OMH setup — evidence that long-lived agent workloads now sustain serious usage at the top end. For builders, the [**dag ulw** skill walkthrough](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-1703b33cc71e) is the pick: it plans jobs as a directed acyclic graph of parallel, subagent-owned tasks, and a [fresh speedup this week lets Hermes self-run final checks on small tasks](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-12676651ed0f). A new [**Terminal Desktop & Bot System** release](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-b25e116e62ad) was announced prominently on social — the cycle's only launch — and **@Teknium** stayed highly visible, most notably [asking the community about reusable **audit skills**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-bb63dd857040), a question that lands directly on this week's security theme. His [nudge to point agents at resources to build from](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-0d0565fb83b2) doubles as the most reusable tip of the cycle.

**Security stays the standing action item — carried over, not new.** The malicious NPM package [**leadstack-crm-connect**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50585975), which backdoored machines by installing **Hermes Agent** as root and tasking it remotely over **Telegram**, remains the top research priority by direct relevance, but it was first reported earlier this week: treat it as your standing audit trigger rather than fresh news. The same goes for the [documented deployment gaps](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49977400) — no official **Helm** chart, root-at-init container requirements complicating hardened **Kubernetes** deploys — with community guides ([containerized setups](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50131496), [running Hermes Agent on a VPS to control an old rooted Android phone](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50629729)) still filling the void, and the [custom-**Metal**-kernels-over-**MLX** work](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50648334) on Mac clusters still the week's local-inference performance story.

**Fresh items are thin, and the data says so itself.** The only news-cycle candidate is a [docs refresh of the Hermes Helper Reddit post index](/?date=2026-11-28&category=news#item-8092447747cb) on the **hermes-agent-community** repo — pure housekeeping with no code, features, or fixes, and explicitly flagged as a cut candidate. The official items circulating again today ([**Claude Pro/Max** subscription authentication](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49790991), [**Kanban** multi-agent collaboration docs](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49604068)) are carry-overs from earlier in the week, as are the lower-ranked academic entries ([context engineering](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-2611.30494), [3D agentic reasoning](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-2611.29969), [**AIChipbench**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-2611.33093)). One verification note before you go model-hunting: a circulating thread references "[**GLM 5.3 Flash**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49916751)," which doesn't match Zhipu/Z.ai's current lineup — the latest GLM is **GLM-5.2** — so it's almost certainly a version typo, not a new release.

**Community sentiment is holiday-warm and builder-heavy.** Thanksgiving gratitude led engagement: the official [thank-you to **Hermeticists**](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-b52449528bc4) pulled **1,519 likes**, [**@Teknium**'s greeting](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-3bfb1267f58c) **602**, and [**@rlaope**'s striking "hermes" image](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-a222dd010d7c) **310**. Reddit contributed no items this cycle. Screened from coverage: three Black Friday SEO/backlink promotional posts and one link-only reply to **@Albinkultur**, excluded over a corrupted record ID in the source data.

Executive Summary

The "Sooon" tease cashed out as a Black Friday deal. @NousResearch's 24-hour offer — 50% off the first month of Nous Portal plans with code FIFTYFIFTY — drew the batch's biggest reach at 134k+ views and 893 likes, and it's the payoff to last cycle's Portal name-drop and "imminent reveal" tease. Two official clarifications matter at checkout: the exclamation mark is not part of the code, and the discount applies to the first month only. If you've been waiting for a cheaper on-ramp to the Portal ecosystem, this is the 24-hour window.

The Oh My Hermes ecosystem keeps compounding. @rlaope's OMH plugin is nearing 6.2k GitHub stars (up from 6.1k reported yesterday), and the standout data point is a power-user report of burning 200B tokens/month on Hermes-Agent through an OMH setup — evidence that long-lived agent workloads now sustain serious usage at the top end. For builders, the dag ulw skill walkthrough is the pick: it plans jobs as a directed acyclic graph of parallel, subagent-owned tasks, and a fresh speedup this week lets Hermes self-run final checks on small tasks. A new Terminal Desktop & Bot System release was announced prominently on social — the cycle's only launch — and @Teknium stayed highly visible, most notably asking the community about reusable audit skills, a question that lands directly on this week's security theme. His nudge to point agents at resources to build from doubles as the most reusable tip of the cycle.

Security stays the standing action item — carried over, not new. The malicious NPM package leadstack-crm-connect, which backdoored machines by installing Hermes Agent as root and tasking it remotely over Telegram, remains the top research priority by direct relevance, but it was first reported earlier this week: treat it as your standing audit trigger rather than fresh news. The same goes for the documented deployment gaps — no official Helm chart, root-at-init container requirements complicating hardened Kubernetes deploys — with community guides (containerized setups, running Hermes Agent on a VPS to control an old rooted Android phone) still filling the void, and the custom-Metal-kernels-over-MLX work on Mac clusters still the week's local-inference performance story.

Fresh items are thin, and the data says so itself. The only news-cycle candidate is a docs refresh of the Hermes Helper Reddit post index on the hermes-agent-community repo — pure housekeeping with no code, features, or fixes, and explicitly flagged as a cut candidate. The official items circulating again today (Claude Pro/Max subscription authentication, Kanban multi-agent collaboration docs) are carry-overs from earlier in the week, as are the lower-ranked academic entries (context engineering, 3D agentic reasoning, AIChipbench). One verification note before you go model-hunting: a circulating thread references "GLM 5.3 Flash," which doesn't match Zhipu/Z.ai's current lineup — the latest GLM is GLM-5.2 — so it's almost certainly a version typo, not a new release.

Community sentiment is holiday-warm and builder-heavy. Thanksgiving gratitude led engagement: the official thank-you to Hermeticists pulled 1,519 likes, @Teknium's greeting 602, and @rlaope's striking "hermes" image 310. Reddit contributed no items this cycle. Screened from coverage: three Black Friday SEO/backlink promotional posts and one link-only reply to @Albinkultur, excluded over a corrupted record ID in the source data.

top_topics.name: Hermes Plugin Ecosystem
top_topics.description: Community-built tooling around Hermes Agent is flourishing, led by the [Oh My Hermes (OMH) plugin approaching 6.2k GitHub stars](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-86e1892603b8), alongside [Comemo (composite memory provider fanning out writes)](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50518538), [Refine Cycle (self-improvement plugin)](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49606988), [Hermes-Voice (Home Assistant integration)](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50381927), [Paper Harness (native SwiftUI iPhone client)](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50278175), [ClusterMob (profile registry)](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50197497), and lightweight orchestrators like [shoebox](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-50610136) and [Verso](/?date=2026-11-28&category=research#item-hn-49628094). Power-user scale is notable, with one OMH setup reportedly [burning 200B tokens per month on Hermes-Agent](/?date=2026-11-28&category=social#item-4db7a63d92b6). Founder visibility and official support replies reinforce a warm, builder-heavy ecosystem.

The incident highlights the risks of root-level agent installs and trusting third-party packages.

oh-my-hermes turns Hermes into a graph engineer, and as of this week it's a faster one.

oh-my-herme...
top_items.content:
oh-my-hermes turns Hermes into a graph engineer, and as of this week it's a faster one.

oh-my-hermes is a plugin for Hermes Agent. Give it a big job and it plans the work as a graph, sends each piece to the subagent and model that fits it, runs independent pieces in parallel, and doesn't call the job done until a separate check passes on the real output.

Small jobs used to pay the full price anyway: one more agent at the end just to run a single check, plus a round trip for every piece that finished. Now Hermes runs that final check itself and closes finished pieces together. One less agent, fewer waits, same guardrails.

Big jobs still get the full graph.

If you're running Hermes:
https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

top_items.content:
If you hand Oh-My-Hermes a big job without typing "dag ulw", you're doing it the slow way.

https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

"dag ulw" is a skill in oh-my-hermes. The dag is the graph the work gets split into. ulw is ultrawork: the agent carries the whole job to the end with its subagents instead of stopping to ask you at every step.

oh-my-hermes is the workflow layer for Hermes Agent, an all-in-one package. It has long-term memory, expert skills that keep getting updated (a router picks the right one, so they cost nothing until you need them), tuning per model, and this.
